title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web
focus: Explain the PageRank of a small web graph (Section 2.4 / 2.5). The learner edits which pages link to which in a 4-page graph and changes the damping factor d. Show the link graph, the transition matrix, the rank of each page after power iteration, and how ranks change over iterations. Guide them through a page with many incoming links and a page that links to nobody (dangling node). Check that ranks sum to 1 and that a symmetric graph gives equal ranks.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows matrices and basic probability
excerpt:
2.4 Definition of PageRank

Let u be a web page. Then let F_u be the set of pages u points to and B_u be the set of pages that point to u. Let N_u = |F_u| be the number of links from u and let c be a factor used for normalization (so that the total rank of all web pages is constant). We begin by defining a simple ranking, R which is a slightly simplified version of PageRank:

R(u) = c Σ_{v ∈ B_u} R(v) / N_v

This formalizes the intuition in the previous section. Note that the rank of a page is divided among its forward links evenly to contribute to the ranks of the pages they point to.

The equation is recursive but it may be computed by starting with any set of ranks and iterating the computation until it converges.

2.5 Random Surfer Model

The definition of PageRank above has another intuitive basis in random walks on graphs. The simplified version corresponds to the standing probability distribution of a random walk on the graph of the Web. Intuitively, this can be thought of as modeling the behavior of a "random surfer". The "random surfer" simply keeps clicking on successive links at random. However, if a real Web surfer ever gets into a small loop of web pages, it is unlikely that the surfer will continue in the loop forever. Instead, the surfer will jump to some other page.

2.7 Dangling Links

One issue with this model is dangling links. Dangling links are simply links that point to any page with no outgoing links. They affect the model because it is not clear where their weight should be distributed.
